items.followUp: Which mosquito transmits malaria to humans, and which disease is commonly transmitted by Culex?

rubric.why: Identifies the mosquito that transmits malaria.
rubric.description: States that female Anopheles transmits malaria.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly linking Anopheles with malaria.

rubric.why: Distinguishes Culex from the malaria vector.
rubric.description: States that Culex transmits filariasis (elephantiasis), not malaria.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly linking Culex with filariasis.

modelAnswer: Female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit malaria to humans.
Culex mosquitoes transmit filariasis, not malaria.

items.followUp: Write down any four features of a scientific theory.

rubric.why: Rewards two valid characteristics of a good hypothesis.
rubric.description: Gives any two characteristics, such as being testable, based on observations, simple and clear, or explaining observations.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two distinct correct characteristics.

rubric.why: Rewards the remaining two requested characteristics.
rubric.description: Gives two further valid characteristics of a good hypothesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two additional distinct correct characteristics.

items.followUp: Name the three levels at which biodiversity is commonly described.

rubric.why: Checks the core meaning of biodiversity.
rubric.description: Defines biodiversity as the variety of living organisms or life forms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the basic definition.

rubric.why: Checks recognition of the main levels of biodiversity.
rubric.description: Mentions genetic, species and ecosystem diversity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for all three levels.

modelAnswer: Biodiversity is the variety of living organisms in a particular area or on Earth.
It includes genetic diversity, species diversity and ecosystem diversity.

items.followUp: State two ways biological classification helps scientists study organisms.

rubric.why: One main aim of classification is to identify organisms.
rubric.description: States that classification helps identify organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying organisms as an aim.

rubric.why: Classification arranges organisms into groups and makes their study easier.
rubric.description: States that classification groups organisms to make their study easier.

modelAnswer: It arranges organisms into groups, making them easier to study.

items.followUp: Differentiate between the inner and outer membranes of a mitochondrion.

rubric.why: Cristae are the folds of the mitochondrial inner membrane.
rubric.description: Defines cristae as folds of the inner mitochondrial membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct location and structure of cristae.

rubric.why: Cisternae are flattened membranous sacs, commonly described as parts of the endoplasmic reticulum.
rubric.description: Defines cisternae as flattened membranous sacs of the endoplasmic reticulum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct structure and location of cisternae.

modelAnswer: Cristae are folds of the inner membrane of mitochondria.
Cisternae are flattened membranous sacs of the endoplasmic reticulum.

items.followUp: What is simple diffusion, and how does it differ from facilitated diffusion?

rubric.why: Facilitated diffusion moves substances down their concentration gradient.
rubric.description: States that substances move from higher to lower concentration, without energy input.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the direction of movement and/or that no energy is required.

rubric.why: The defining feature is transport through membrane proteins.
rubric.description: States that substances cross the membrane through channel or carrier proteins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the membrane proteins involved.

modelAnswer: Facilitated diffusion is the passive movement of substances across a cell membrane from higher to lower concentration.
The substances pass through channel or carrier proteins and no cellular energy is used.

items.followUp: What happens to chromosome number when nondisjunction occurs during meiosis?

rubric.why: Disjunction is the normal separation of chromosomes during cell division.
rubric.description: States that chromosomes or chromatids separate and move to opposite poles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the normal separation.

rubric.why: Nondisjunction is a failure of normal chromosome separation and can produce cells with abnormal chromosome numbers.
rubric.description: States that chromosomes fail to separate, causing abnormal chromosome numbers in the resulting cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the failure to separate and its consequence.

modelAnswer: In disjunction, chromosomes or chromatids separate and move to opposite poles during cell division.
In nondisjunction, they fail to separate properly, producing cells with abnormal chromosome numbers.

items.followUp: Why is apoptosis important in the development and maintenance of an organism?

rubric.why: Apoptosis is the regulated process of cell death.
rubric.description: Defines apoptosis as programmed or controlled cell death.

rubric.why: Apoptosis removes cells that are damaged or no longer needed.
rubric.description: States that apoptosis removes damaged or unnecessary cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct role of apoptosis.

modelAnswer: Apoptosis is programmed, controlled cell death.
It removes damaged or unneeded cells from an organism.
